_note: The first film (14 min, 21 scenes) grows language by language like the site (관리자 2026-11-13). Policy in words: motion/youtube/LANGUAGES.md §4-1. This file is the machine-readable part; `node motion/youtube/film14.mjs status` reads it with uploaded.json and the files on disk and prints each language's NEXT step. Video ids live in uploaded.json only (global.film[<lang>] = music horizontal, global.film['<lang>-v'] = music vertical, global.film['<lang>-narr'] / ['<lang>-narr-v'] = narrated; Korean: film.ko / film['ko-narr'] / film['ko-v'] / film['ko-narr-v']).

rules.rule: Every film language gets the 14-min MUSIC version HORIZONTAL and the 21 scene Shorts cut from the vertical render (관리자 2026-11-13: "가로세로 세로 만든 걸 쇼츠로 기본"; then "쇼츠를 무조건 만들기로 했으니까 가로편이 있으니 세로 14분을 올릴 필요는 없겠다" — abroad the Shorts feed is the only door; 10/26–11/13 the intl channel got 1,084 views from the Shorts feed, the 14-min films 0–4 each). No vertical 14-min upload. Made on GitHub: node motion/film-lang.mjs ci <lang> --steps "h v kit release". The vfull step (whole film in portrait) stays available but is not part of the plan. Shorts go out in waves (global-move.mjs), one scene a day at local 19:00.

Languages ElevenLabs speaks well get a NARRATED version: 14-min horizontal AND 21 narrated scene Shorts (no vertical 14-min). It becomes the language's main video: the site's film button (FILM_YT), first item of the language playlist, the related video of that language's Shorts, end screens. Shorts (관리자 2026-11-13 "응 그렇게해줘"): if the language's music Shorts are not yet public, the narrated Shorts replace the unpublished ones (as Korean 7–21 did); if the music Shorts have already run, the narrated Shorts go out as a second run about a month after the music run ended (the same picture re-posted at once can be treated as repetitive content). Music Shorts are never deleted. Narrated Shorts carry that language's narration captions at the top of the picture (as the Korean narrated Shorts).

Before a narrated version is made: (1) Scripture read aloud is allowed for that translation (scripture_audio = ok, with source), (2) the translated narration script passed the site's prose gate (verify-prose back-translation + native review, report motion/reviews/<lang>-narr.md with no open BLOCKER/MAJOR), (3) a 1-minute pilot was approved by the maintainer, (4) after generation, the transcription matches the script (film14.mjs narr-verify).

Captions are a by-product of translation: on-screen text → motion/subs/<lang>/film-h.srt (film-v.srt for the vertical version: same scene lengths, but the portrait layouts break lines differently, so the cue times differ), narration → motion/narration/<lang>-narr.vtt. On-screen-text captions go on the Korean MUSIC version (every language) and on that language's own music version (search). Narration captions go on the Korean NARRATED version (only languages with a translated narration — on-screen text does not match the voice) and on that language's narrated version. film14.mjs captions uploads what is missing.

Music version → narrated version link; the narrated version never links back to the music version. Every video links the other languages and the series (xlinks.mjs). No language counts in descriptions or comments.

Where we uploaded our own captions in a language, YouTube's automatic track in that language is deleted right after the upload (yt-api asr-off) — standing OK from the maintainer 2026-11-13 ('자동자막 앞으로는 빼자'), no need to ask each time. Irreversible, so only where our own track exists.
Never YouTube auto-dub / auto-translate; every translation goes through our pipeline.

narr._note: Per language: elevenlabs = speaks it well (yes/no/unknown — check creative_get_model_guide for the model and judge the pilot), scripture_audio = permission to read that Bible translation aloud in a public video (ok/no/unknown + source), pilot = none/made/approved (+ file), script = motion/narration/<lang>.json. ko is done (2026-10-29).
